thread:
maria: Quick summary from my local runs integrating FlashAttention v3 into the runtime. Posting raw notes and a proposed canary plan.

aj: Curious — did you compare v3 vs v2 on short sequences (<=128) and long (>=1024)?

maria: Yes. Short seq: v3 is ~6% faster p50 token latency, p95 ~3% better. Long seq: weirdly v3 regresses ~2-4% p95 in some configs.

samir: Dumping profiler snippet:
```
kernel: flash_v3_fused
seq_len: 128
gpu_util: 72%
p50_token_ms: 1.2
p95_token_ms: 3.4

kernel: flash_v2_fallback
seq_len: 1024
gpu_util: 85%
p50_token_ms: 6.1
p95_token_ms: 15.8
```
Notes: v3 chooses different tiling at seq_len boundaries; fallback paths trigger extra memcpy for paged KV.

grace: Re: paged KV — we saw similar before: when a request spans page boundaries the kernel does a copy+merge. That kills p95 on long tails.

oliver: Can we route long sequences to v2 until we fix paged-KV prefetching? Kernel selection can be policy-based.

maria: Proposed kernel selector heuristic (pseudo):
```
if seq_len <= 256 and batch_tokens_per_gpu < 1e6:
  prefer flash_v3_fused
elif seq_len > 512:
  prefer flash_v2_stable
else:
  choose by model_arch + quant_level + measured_latency
```
We should also consider kv_page_hits metric to decide.

aj: What about batching heuristics? v3 seems more sensitive to batch shape.

samir: Right. For v3 we should bias towards "shape-coherent" batching (group similar seq_len). Proposed buckets: [<=64, 65-256, 257-512, >512]. Merge policy: allow max batch_tokens per kernel = 512k, prefer homogeneous buckets.

grace: Feature flag plan:
```
ff_enable_flash_v3: off (global)
ff_flash_v3_canary_pct: 0.0
ff_flash_v3_routes: []
ff_flash_v3_selector: "tiered-seqlen"
```
Canary rollout steps below.

maria: Canary plan draft:
- Step 0: CI perf-suite & microbench (already run) -> baseline collected.
- Step 1: Internal canary: 1% of hosted traffic, only seq_len <= 256, stable models, 48h.
- Metrics: p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, OOMs, kv_page_copy_rate, gpu_util, error_rate.
- Step 2: 5% canary, include 257-512 bucket, 72h.
- Step 3: 20% canary with automatic rollback triggers.

oliver: Rollback triggers suggestion:
- p95 increase > 7% vs baseline for two consecutive 15m windows
- tokens/sec drop > 8% for two consecutive windows
- any new OOM or CUDA launch failures

samir: CI microbenchmark command I used:
```
./tools/bench_attn --model gpt2-xl --kernel flash_v3 --batch 8 --seq 128 --iters 200
```
Attach: perf-bot posted the CI job id and summary below.

perf-bot: CI-perf job 2026-03-10-78654 completed. Summary: flash_v3 microbench vs flash_v2: median improvement 5.8% overall, worst-case regression 3.9% observed on GC-heavy runs. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/2026/03/10/78654

maria: Action items:
- samir: investigate paged-KV copy path for v3 and try prefetch + merge optimization.
- oliver: add selector config and feature flag plumbing to runtime.
- grace: build canary dashboard showing kv_page_copy_rate + seq_len distribution + kernel mix.
- aj: update rollout doc and test rollback automation on staging.

aj: Quick Q: do we need a separate quantization path for v3? Some INT8 kernels behave differently.

samir: Good point. v3 fused path requires aligned input shapes; quantized kernels sometimes fall back to slower path. I'll add a quant_compat check in selector.

grace: Also note: update ops telemetry to include `kernel_variant` and `kv_page_hits` per request. That will make post-rollout analysis possible.

maria: OK. If nobody objects I'll flip ff_flash_v3_canary_pct to 1% for short seq next week and run 48h.

oliver: +1
aj: +1
samir: +1
perf-bot: scheduled canary deploy at 2026-03-17T02:30Z

maria: Thanks all — I'll drop these notes in the PR and the rollout doc. If we hit regressions we'll revert the flag and roll back traffic immediately. :thumbsup:
